title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem in the circuit for the oil pressure sensor, so it can't trust the oil pressure reading.
symptoms: Oil pressure gauge reads zero, maxed out or jumps around
Oil pressure light on or flickering
Check engine light on

causes.name: Faulty oil pressure sensor or switch
Oil-soaked, loose or corroded connector, or damaged wiring
Low oil level or real low oil pressure

checks: Check the oil level first
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring for oil, corrosion or damage
fix: Usually a new oil pressure sensor or a connector repair, once real oil pressure is confirmed good.
drive: Check the oil level as soon as you can safely stop. If the oil pressure light is on, the oil is low or you hear ticking or knocking, shut the engine off and don't drive; low oil pressure can wreck an engine in minutes. If the oil is full and the engine sounds normal, get it checked soon.
test_first: Check the oil level, then confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before replacing the sensor. Inspect the connector and wiring for oil soaking or damage.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
plain: The oil pressure reading doesn't match what the computer expects for the engine speed and temperature.
symptoms: Oil pressure gauge reads zero, maxed out or jumps around
Oil pressure light on or flickering
Check engine light on

causes.name: Low oil level or wrong oil viscosity
Worn oil pump or clogged oil pickup screen

checks: Check the oil level and that the right oil grade is in the engine
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
Compare the sensor reading with the mechanical gauge at idle and higher RPM
fix: Most often a new oil pressure sensor; if real pressure is low, the oil pump or engine needs attention.
examples: Common on GM trucks and SUVs with the 4.8L, 5.3L and 6.0L V8, where the oil pressure sensor often fails
drive: Check the oil level as soon as you can safely stop. If the oil pressure light is on, the oil is low or you hear ticking or knocking, shut the engine off and don't drive; low oil pressure can wreck an engine in minutes. If the oil is full and the engine sounds normal, get it checked soon.
test_first: Check oil level and viscosity and confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge. Replace the sensor only if real pressure is good; low pressure points to the pump, pickup or bearings.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage
plain: The oil pressure sensor signal voltage is lower than it should ever be, which usually means a wiring short or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Oil pressure gauge reads zero, maxed out or jumps around
Oil pressure light on or flickering
Check engine light on

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Check the oil level first
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
Check reference voltage and ground at the sensor connector
fix: Usually a new oil pressure sensor or a wiring repair.
drive: Check the oil level as soon as you can safely stop. If the oil pressure light is on, the oil is low or you hear ticking or knocking, shut the engine off and don't drive; low oil pressure can wreck an engine in minutes. If the oil is full and the engine sounds normal, get it checked soon.
test_first: Check the sensor's reference voltage and signal wire for a short to ground, inspect the connector, and confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before replacing the sensor.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch High Voltage
plain: The oil pressure sensor signal voltage is higher than it should ever be, which usually means a broken wire, bad ground or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Oil pressure gauge reads zero, maxed out or jumps around
Oil pressure light on or flickering
Check engine light on

causes.name: Broken wire or poor ground in the sensor circuit

checks: Check the oil level and confirm real oil pressure with a gauge
Inspect the connector and check ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a new oil pressure sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
plain: The computer sees engine oil pressure below a safe level. Driving with low oil pressure can destroy an engine quickly.
symptoms: Oil pressure warning light on
Low or zero reading on the oil pressure gauge
Ticking or knocking from the engine
Check engine light on

causes.name: Wrong oil viscosity or badly overdue oil change
Worn oil pump or clogged oil pickup screen
Faulty oil pressure sensor giving a false low reading

checks: Pull over, shut the engine off and check the oil level
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before driving further
Check the oil condition and filter for sludge or metal
fix: Top up or change the oil first; if pressure is truly low, the oil pump or engine bearings need repair. If real pressure is fine, replace the sensor.
drive: Pull over safely and shut the engine off. Driving with low oil pressure can destroy the engine in minutes. Check the oil once it's off; if it was low and topping up clears the light with no noise, drive gently to a shop. If the light stays on or you hear knocking, have it towed.
test_first: Check the oil level and condition, then measure real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge to rule out a bad sensor before condemning the oil pump, pickup screen or bearings.

title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The part that works the throttle for cruise control isn't responding the way the computer expects.
symptoms: Cruise control not working or cutting out
Check engine light on

causes.name: Faulty cruise control servo or electronic throttle body
Sticking or binding cruise cable (older vehicles)

checks: Inspect the servo wiring and connector
Check the cruise cable and throttle for binding
fix: Usually a cruise servo or throttle body repair, or a wiring fix.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the cooling fan speed sensor. This part reports how fast the engine cooling fan is spinning.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Cooling fan may run constantly or seem weak
Engine may run warm in traffic

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the cooling fan speed sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new cooling fan speed sensor if it tests bad.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The cooling fan speed sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part reports how fast the engine cooling fan is spinning.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Cooling fan may run constantly or seem weak
Engine may run warm in traffic

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish cooling fan speed sensor
Worn or dragging cooling fan or fan clutch
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the cooling fan speed sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Check the fan and fan clutch for wear, wobble or drag
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new cooling fan speed sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
plain: The computer is not getting any signal from the sensor that reports how fast the engine cooling fan is spinning.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Cooling fan may run constantly or seem weak
Engine may run warm in traffic

causes.name: Fan not turning at all (failed fan clutch or motor)

checks: Confirm the fan actually turns when it should
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fan speed sensor; a new fan clutch or motor if the fan is not turning.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the cooling fan speed sensor keeps cutting in and out or jumping around. This part reports how fast the engine cooling fan is spinning.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Cooling fan may run constantly or seem weak
Engine may run warm in traffic

causes.name: Chafed wiring that shorts or opens over bumps

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data on a scan tool
Look for chafed wires near hot or moving parts
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new cooling fan speed sensor if it tests bad.

title: Cold Start "A" Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
plain: Right after a cold start, the "A" camshaft on bank 1 was further ahead (advanced) than the computer commanded. This is part of the variable valve timing system.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or hesitation right after a cold start
Possible rattle at startup

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-grade engine oil
Sticking or faulty variable valve timing solenoid

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Check for other camshaft timing or correlation codes
Test the timing solenoid and check cam timing on a scan tool
fix: Often an oil change with the correct oil or a new timing solenoid; a stretched chain or worn phaser needs a timing job.

title: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Regulator Valve Performance
plain: The valve that controls how much oil vapor is drawn out of the engine's crankcase isn't working as expected.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or whistling noise
Possible oil leaks or oil consumption

causes.name: Faulty PCV valve or oil separator

checks: Inspect the PCV valve, oil separator and hoses
Check for vacuum leaks around the valve cover
fix: Usually a new PCV valve, oil separator or valve cover with built-in PCV.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor. This part tells the computer the pressure in the A/C system.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm or cutting in and out
Check engine light on

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C refrigerant pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The A/C refrigerant pressure sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part tells the computer the pressure in the A/C system.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm or cutting in and out
Check engine light on

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish A/C refrigerant pressure sensor
Refrigerant charge too low or too high
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Check A/C pressures with a gauge set
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new A/C refrigerant pressure sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
plain: The A/C pressure sensor signal is too low. A low reading often means the system is low on refrigerant, but it can also be the sensor or its wiring.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm air
A/C compressor not turning on
Check engine light on

causes.name: Signal wire shorted to ground or corroded connector
Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Check A/C system pressures with a gauge set
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check reference voltage and ground at the sensor
fix: Either a new A/C pressure sensor or a leak repair and recharge, depending on what the gauges show.
drive: Generally safe to keep driving; it mainly affects the air conditioning. If you rely on the A/C to clear a fogged windshield, make sure you can still see clearly before driving. Get it checked when convenient.
test_first: Measure actual refrigerant pressure with gauges and leak test, then check the sensor's reference voltage, signal wire and connector before replacing the sensor.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
plain: The signal from the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor is higher than it should ever be, which usually points to a broken wire, bad ground or a failed sensor. This part tells the computer the pressure in the A/C system.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm or cutting in and out
Check engine light on

causes.name: Broken wire or poor ground in the sensor circuit
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for broken wires or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C refrigerant pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Air Conditioner Refrigerant Charge Loss
plain: The computer thinks the A/C system has lost much of its refrigerant, usually from a leak.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm air
A/C compressor cycling on and off quickly or not running

causes.name: Refrigerant leak at a hose, seal, condenser or evaporator
Faulty A/C pressure or temperature sensor

checks: Check A/C pressures with a gauge set
Leak-test with dye or an electronic detector
fix: Find and fix the leak, then evacuate and recharge the system.

title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the A/C evaporator temperature sensor. This part tells the computer how cold the A/C evaporator is so it does not freeze up.
symptoms: A/C blowing warm or cutting out
A/C may ice up and lose airflow

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the A/C evaporator temperature sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C evaporator temperature sensor if it tests bad.

fix: Usually a new A/C evaporator temperature sensor, after ruling out wiring.

title: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Heater Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the PCV heater. This part warms the crankcase vent so moisture cannot freeze it shut in cold weather.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
In freezing weather, possible oil leaks from a frozen vent

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the PCV heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the PCV heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new PCV heater if it tests bad.

title: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Heater Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the PCV heater, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part warms the crankcase vent so moisture cannot freeze it shut in cold weather.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
In freezing weather, possible oil leaks from a frozen vent
checks: Inspect the PCV heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the PCV heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new PCV heater if it tests bad.

title: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Heater Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the PCV heater, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part warms the crankcase vent so moisture cannot freeze it shut in cold weather.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
In freezing weather, possible oil leaks from a frozen vent
checks: Inspect the PCV heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the PCV heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new PCV heater if it tests bad.
